newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index closes up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index closes up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Monday in slow trading, with investors adjusting their positions on the basis of firms' interim results, brokers said. The index ended up 0.172 point or 0.33 percent to 51.581 points, on volume of 6.1 million shares worth $2.1 million. Of 41 B shares, 36 traded, with nine up, 16 flat and 11 down.

Brokers said institutions were seen adjusting holdings today after all Shanghai-listed companies finished posting interim results by the end of August, preventing the index from moving sharply up and down. Many retail investors stayed on the sidelines, resulting in dull trading.
"Stocks in companies with good results were the market focus today," one broker said.
"Technical charts show the index will rebound this week," said a second trader.
Tientsin Marine Shipping was today's star performer on its good prospects, rising $0.014 or 4.37 percent to $0.334, on volume of 488,900 shares.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Product traded the most on overseas selling, shedding $0.006 or 1.20 percent to $0.490, on volume of 851,100 shares.
China Textile Machinery was the biggest loser on poor results, falling $0.006 or 5.00 percent to $0.114, on volume of 10,000 shares.

Shanghai's A share index ended down, with capital flowing out to the Shenzhen bourse, which was boosted by news reports that a meeting of exchange members was likely to work out measures to support the market, brokers said.
It lost 5.618 points or 0.66 percent to 841.592 points, on volume of 339.6 million shares worth 2.6 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index closed down 26.018 points or 1.20 percent to 2148.547 points.

Tonghua Tongbao Medicine was the biggest loser after the firm denied a rumour that it would shortly issue convertible bonds, brokers said. It fell 1.33 yuan or 8.96 percent to 13.50 yuan, on volume of 3.4 million shares.
The rumour had pushed up the stock price sharply up since early last week.
